```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.8, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%")
library(postrank)
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank",
  mustWork = TRUE), local = TRUE)
one <- load_or_compute("tutorial_one")
two <- load_or_compute("tutorial_two")
frontier <- load_or_compute("tutorial_frontier")
sensitivity <- load_or_compute("tutorial_sensitivity")
commonality <- load_or_compute("tutorial_commonality")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 4L) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
pct <- function(x, digits = 1L) paste0(fmt(100 * x, digits), "%")
sci <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 2L)
ev <- two$evaluation
reference_tau <- two$settings$tau
reference_cap <- two$settings$G_max
st <- sensitivity$table
sg <- sensitivity$grid
ch <- sensitivity$changes
ref_row <- match(sensitivity$reference_id, sg$setting_id)
hi_row <- which(sg$tau > reference_tau)
cap4_row <- which(sg$G_max > reference_cap)
heavy_row <- which(sg$w_score_A > two$settings$weights[["score_A"]])
ct <- commonality$table
stopifnot(length(hi_row) == 1L, length(cap4_row) == 1L,
  length(heavy_row) == 1L, identical(st$setting_id, sg$setting_id),
  identical(ch$setting_id, sg$setting_id), ev$N == st$N[ref_row])
```

Graphical summaries distinguish uncertainty in entity scores from the
comparisons disclosed by a grading. Sensitivity analyses additionally
examine how that grading changes with the withholding cost, criterion
weights or grade cap.

We use the six fictional sites in
[Analysis with one or several criteria](a1-getting-started.html). Their scores have specified
normal laws in illustrative standardized units, with standard deviation
`r fmt(sqrt(pr_tutorial$law$covariance[1L, 1L, 1L]), 1L)`.
Sites are independent, as are the scores within each site. These laws are
not fitted to observations. Larger values receive higher priority on both
criteria, and grade 1 has highest priority.

The reference analysis assigns equal criterion weights, permits at most
`r reference_cap` grades and sets the withholding cost `tau` to
`r fmt(reference_tau, 1L)`. It groups A through D together, followed by E
and then F. The analyses and settings sweeps were prepared using HiGHS.
Rendering reads those results, evaluates fixed alternatives and produces
figures without an optimizer. Optional recomputation calls are displayed
without execution.

## Graphical representations {#choose-a-figure-by-the-question}

The seven plotting functions return `ggplot` objects based on prepared
results. A change in graphical representation therefore leaves the selected
grading unchanged.

| Quantity or comparison | Function and what it shows |
|:--|:--|
| Target estimates and uncertainty | `postrank_plot_report_card()`: target means, marginal intervals and grade membership. |
| Disclosed and withheld pair relations | `postrank_plot_relations()`: selected relations, or changes between two reports. |
| Error probability for a potential direction | `postrank_plot_pairwise()`: criterion-specific probabilities of an error if the row is placed above the column. |
| Criterion-specific expected errors | `postrank_plot_profile()`: expected error rates or risk for the selected grades. |
| Variation with the withholding cost | `postrank_plot_frontier()`: disclosure, error and risk along a prepared cost grid. |
| Evaluation of alternative grade vectors | `postrank_plot_compare()`: reports evaluated under a common loss, or their relation changes. |
| Criterion-specific cost of common grades | `postrank_plot_commonality()`: extra criterion risk relative to its own optimized report. |

Report cards and pairwise probabilities summarize the posterior, whereas
relation maps represent selected reporting actions. A pale pairwise cell
may support a direction whose comparison is withheld by the grading, and
shared grades do not assert score equality. This distinction is illustrated
in the [chronic-absence example](a2-cde-accountability.html).

For large analyses, the displayed subset and its selection rule should be
specified. Report cards use `entities` and `max_rows`, whereas pairwise
plots use `entities` and `max_entities`. Named `entity_labels` and
`criterion_labels` change display labels while retaining identifiers and
values. Setting `ncol = 1` arranges criterion panels vertically for narrow
formats. Subset figures still refer to the original report; they do not
refit or optimize the subset.

## Error rates and denominators {#read-the-error-denominator-first}

```{r labels}
library(postrank)
sites <- pr_tutorial
entity_labels <- setNames(sites$units$label, sites$units$entity_id)
criterion_labels <- c(score_A = "Score A", score_B = "Score B")
```

The common grading discloses `r ev$N` of `r ev$M` unordered pairs. Each
criterion's expected error count is divided by this same number of
disclosed pairs in the default profile. The resulting rates can differ
even under equal criterion weights.

```{r profile, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap="Expected wrong-direction errors per disclosed pair for the prepared common grading. Both criteria use the same disclosed comparisons; point size represents criterion weight."}
profile_plot <- postrank_plot_profile(two, show = "E_over_N",
  criterion_labels = criterion_labels)
profile_plot
```

```{r profile-data}
profile_data <- postrank_plot_data(two, "profile")
profile_data[, c("criterion", "weight", "E", "E_over_N", "E_over_M")]
```

Expected errors per disclosed pair are
`r pct(profile_data$E_over_N[1L], 2L)` for score A and
`r pct(profile_data$E_over_N[2L], 2L)` for score B. `E_over_M` instead uses
all `r ev$M` pairs as its denominator. Both quantities are posterior
expectations rather than observed error counts. Criterion risk additionally
includes the cost of the `r ev$M - ev$N` withheld pairs and is displayed by
`show = "risk"`.

When every comparison is withheld, `E/N` is undefined and the profile
omits the point with an explanation. The absence of a valid grading is
likewise represented by its status. Unavailable frontier results interrupt
lines. Empty panels must therefore be interpreted from these recorded
states rather than as evidence of agreement or precision.

## Changes to reporting settings {#vary-one-reporting-choice-at-a-time}

The settings grid distinguishes three changes to the decision problem.
Changing `tau` alters the cost of withholding; changing criterion weights
alters the relative contribution of errors; changing only the grade cap
changes the admissible reports under a fixed loss. The posterior score
distributions remain fixed throughout. Weights combine criterion-specific
losses rather than defining a composite score to be ranked.

```{r settings-grid}
grid <- postrank_settings_grid(two$settings,
  tau = c(.1, .3), G_max = c(2L, 4L),
  weights = list(
    A_heavy = c(score_A = .8, score_B = .2),
    B_heavy = c(score_A = .2, score_B = .8)
  ))
```

The default grid varies one supplied axis at a time around the reference,
giving `r nrow(sg)` settings here rather than their full cross-product.
The optional call below recomputes these reports from the same posterior
input. Displayed results use the stored sweep's grid and are matched by
setting ID.

```{r optional-sensitivity, eval=FALSE}
sensitivity <- postrank_sensitivity(two, grid, backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304))
```

```{r settings-table, echo=FALSE}
settings_table <- data.frame(
  Setting = sg$label, tau = sg$tau, Cap = sg$G_max,
  `Weights A/B` = paste(fmt(sg$w_score_A, 1L), fmt(sg$w_score_B, 1L), sep = "/"),
  Grades = st$G, Disclosed = st$N,
  `A errors/N` = pct(st$E_over_N_score_A, 2L),
  `B errors/N` = pct(st$E_over_N_score_B, 2L), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(settings_table, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "One choice varies at a time. Errors/N is the posterior expected error proportion among the comparisons disclosed by that row's report.")
```

Assigning weight `r fmt(sg$w_score_A[heavy_row], 1L)` to score A reduces its
expected error proportion among disclosed pairs to
`r pct(st$E_over_N_score_A[heavy_row], 2L)`, while that for score B increases
to `r pct(st$E_over_N_score_B[heavy_row], 2L)`. This change follows from the
specified relative importance of errors, with the precision of the score-A
posterior held fixed. A weight also differs from a constraint limiting an
error proportion.

Increasing the cap to `r sg$G_max[cap4_row]` gives a report with
`r st$G[cap4_row]` grades and changes
`r ev$M - ch$n_same[cap4_row]` pair relations. An additional permitted grade
need not be occupied. The effect depends on the posterior and loss rather
than implying a fixed increase in the number of comparisons.

All these stored rows have numerical status `optimal`, with maximum recorded
risk gap `r sci(max(st$risk_absolute_gap))`.
`r sum(grepl("clamped", st$bound_source))` rows record a small correction
where a solver lower bound exceeded the evaluated action loss within the
objective tolerance. The bound source and warnings remain in the result.
These are optimization statements about the supplied probabilities, not
posterior intervals or guarantees about the score model.

## Withholding-cost path {#follow-the-withholding-cost-path}

The withholding-cost path holds criterion weights and the grade cap fixed
while varying `tau`. The optional call specifies the prepared grid shown
below.

```{r optional-frontier, eval=FALSE}
frontier <- postrank_frontier(two, tau = c(.05, .1, .2, .3, .4),
  backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304))
```

```{r frontier, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Prepared withholding-cost path with fixed equal weights and a fixed grade cap. The dashed line marks the reference cost. Each risk panel value uses its own tau; the lines connect computed settings and are not interpolated grade reports."}
frontier_plot <- postrank_plot_frontier(frontier, highlight = reference_tau)
frontier_plot
```

The disclosure counts along the grid are
`r paste(frontier$table$N, collapse = ", ")`. A greater withholding cost
favors additional disclosure. For exact optima under the same posterior,
weights and admissible reports, the disclosure count is nondecreasing in
`tau`. The finite grid may omit change points, and numerical solver statuses
alone do not establish the exact property.

For score B, the error proportion increases from the reference to the next
withholding cost, then decreases at the final cost as the groups change.
Neither criterion-specific error proportion is required to be monotone.
The risk panel evaluates a different loss at each cost; its increase cannot
be interpreted as deterioration on a common accuracy scale. Lines connect
evaluated settings for display and do not define fractional grades between
them.

Nondecreasing disclosure counts do not require nested sets of comparisons.
At `tau =` `r fmt(sg$tau[hi_row], 1L)`, the report newly discloses
`r ch$n_new_disclosed[hi_row]` pairs and newly withholds
`r ch$n_new_withheld[hi_row]` relative to the reference. The net increase is
`r st$N[hi_row] - ev$N`, although one previously disclosed direction is
removed.

```{r changes, fig.height=5.2, fig.cap="Relation changes from the reference to the next larger withholding cost. Light gray means unchanged, including pairs withheld by both reports; medium gray marks a newly withheld pair."}
higher_cost_fit <- sensitivity$fits[[hi_row]]
changes_plot <- postrank_plot_relations(two, higher_cost_fit,
  entity_labels = entity_labels)
changes_plot
```

## Comparison under a common loss {#compare-alternatives-on-the-same-loss}

Comparison of candidate reports requires evaluation under common posterior
inputs, weights and withholding cost. The score-A-only grading provides an
alternative action, but its original single-criterion risk is not directly
comparable with the common report's two-criterion risk.

```{r compare}
comparison <- postrank_compare(two,
  `Score A grades` = get_grades(one),
  `Withhold all` = setNames(rep(1L, nrow(sites$units)), sites$units$entity_id),
  baselines = character())
```

```{r comparison-table, echo=FALSE}
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Report = c("Common grades", "Score A grades", "Withhold all"),
  Disclosed = comparison$table$N,
  `Risk at reference settings` = fmt(comparison$table$risk),
  `Within grade cap` = comparison$table$family_feasible,
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(comparison_table, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Each supplied action is evaluated under the same two-criterion reference loss. Evaluating an action does not optimize it.")
```

Score A's grades disclose `r comparison$table$N[2L]` pairs and have common-loss
risk `r fmt(comparison$table$risk[2L])`, compared with
`r fmt(comparison$table$risk[1L])` for the common grading.
Both respect the same cap. This comparison concerns these fixed reports and
the stated loss; it does not establish that one score or weighting policy
is scientifically preferable. `postrank_plot_compare(comparison)` presents
these results graphically, retaining each action's computation status and
scope. The relation view displays changes in pairwise decisions; it does
not compare the reports' risks.

## Criterion-specific cost of a common grading {#quantify-the-cost-of-sharing-grades}

`postrank_commonality_cost()` measures the additional criterion-specific
loss associated with a fixed common grading. Each criterion is optimized
separately at the same withholding cost and grade cap, and its loss is
compared with its loss under the common action. No additional error-budget
constraints are imposed here.

```{r optional-commonality, eval=FALSE}
commonality <- postrank_commonality_cost(two, backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304))
```

```{r commonality, fig.height=3.6, fig.cap="Extra criterion risk from using the common grading. The plotted endpoints are derived from each own-criterion solve's incumbent and lower bound; they are not posterior uncertainty intervals."}
commonality_plot <- postrank_plot_commonality(commonality)
commonality_plot
```

For score A, criterion risk under the common report is
`r fmt(ct$common_grade_risk[1L])`, compared with
`r fmt(ct$own_best_risk[1L])` under its best found report, a difference of
`r fmt(ct$cost_lower[1L])`. The corresponding additional risk for score B is
`r fmt(ct$cost_lower[2L])`. These differences are in expected-loss units,
including withholding costs, and do not measure changes in individual
sites' score uncertainty.

The figure retains uncertainty about numerical optimization separately.
The common-action risk minus the own incumbent risk gives the lower endpoint
(truncated at zero); subtracting the own solver lower bound gives the upper
endpoint when available. A large gap in the criterion-specific optimization
can therefore leave the additional loss imprecisely determined. Here the
endpoints nearly coincide. Their width does not
measure posterior variation, sampling uncertainty or model misspecification,
and their interpretation inherits the solver bounds' numerical limitations.

## Figure data and export {#save-the-view-together-with-its-meaning}

`postrank_plot_data()` returns the stored values underlying a figure.
Standard `ggplot2` layers can modify presentation, with label and theme
changes leaving those values unchanged. The following code writes a PNG
profile to a temporary directory and, when the optional `svglite` package is
installed, an SVG version:

```{r save-figures}
figure_dir <- tempfile("postrank-figures-")
dir.create(figure_dir)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, "criterion-profile.png"),
  profile_plot, width = 7, height = 3.5, units = "in", dpi = 300)
if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, "criterion-profile.svg"),
    profile_plot, device = svglite::svglite,
    width = 7, height = 3.5, units = "in")
}
```

Figures intended for a report require a permanent output directory and
inspection at the intended print size. Labels, denominators, selected
entities and legends should remain legible, with captions identifying the
target direction and distinguishing posterior intervals, solver bounds and
withheld comparisons. Retaining the analysis object alongside the figure
preserves its settings and computation status, as described in
[Reading and exporting results](a6-reading-exporting-results.html).

[Computing grades and choosing settings](m5-computing-grades.html) describes how these settings alter the action families and objectives. [Several criteria and competing goals](m2-several-criteria.html) gives the mathematical interpretation of the common-grade cost.
